title: munich solicitations and services - u.s. embassy & consulates in germany
paragraphs: solicitation notice – labor and moving services (munich) reference no.: pr14991437 the u.s. consulate general munich is seeking quotations from qualified companies to establish a blanket purchase agreement (bpa) for labor and moving services within the city of munich and between munich and the government warehouse in maisach. services include loading and unloading, internal relocation of furniture, and transportation of furniture and appliances between government facilities and residences. interested companies are invited to submit quotations in accordance with the requirements outlined in the solicitation package. submission deadline: march 24 – close of business (cob) to receive the full solicitation package, please contact the procurement section at: mostarlice@state.gov please include reference no. pr14991437 in all correspondence regarding this solicitation. ************************************************************************************************************************** u.s. consulate general munich: permanent solicitations the u.s. consulate general munich is permanently seeking commodities and services to maintain its operational functions. all interested providers are invited to tender quotes for the following commodities: commodities: a) heating fuel for various locations within munich between approx. 5,000 to 25,000 liters per delivery should you have interest in any of the above mentioned services, please contact the procurement department in writing. we are interested in companies small and large. this is not a job offer for individuals. please send us a company overview with references to work performed previously. address your interest to: u.s. consulate general, gso / procurement koeniginstrasse 5, 80539 muenchen or send emails to mostarlice@state.gov. ************************************************************************************************************************** important for proposals exceeding $30,000 usd (or the equivalent in local currency), offerors shall be registered in the sam (system for award management) database at https://www.sam.gov prior to submittal of their offer/proposal as prescribed under far 52.204-7 . the guidelines for entity registrations in sam are available at: sam.gov | entity registrations the website compiles standard information such as company legal name, street address, contact information, and what kind of goods and services it offers. to register in sam, an ncage code and a uei number are required. if you do not have this information, it must be obtained before registering. there is no cost involved, neither in obtaining the numbers, nor in registering for sam . interested parties are strongly encouraged to register their business as soon as possible to avoid any delay in making an award to the successful bidder. failure to be registered at time of proposal submission may deem the offeror’s proposal to be considered non-responsible and no further consideration will be given. therefore, offerors are highly encouraged to register immediately if they are interested in submitting a response to many of our requirements. the u.s. government intends to award a contract that is the most advantageous to the government, price and other factors considered. we intend to award a contract based on initial bids, without holding discussions, although we may hold discussions with companies in the comparison range if there is a need to do so. all offerors must be registered in germany, and/or provide full details of any subcontractors! please pay attention to a crucial requirement outlined in the dosar 652.242-73 . this requirement mandates that all vendors possess the necessary licenses and permits to conduct business in germany. it is essential to ensure compliance with all german regulations and legalities to operate successfully in the country. specifically, the german tax authorities expect businesses to obtain a vat-id number and fulfill tax obligations. you should review local laws before submitting a proposal. it is essential that you have knowledge of german actuarial processes and regulations. **************************************************************************************************************************
